headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network access create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors between Devin and Mentat.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can use MCP, browser, shell, and shared integrations; Mentat shares state via filesystem and reads/writes files. That creates a plausible path where Devin’s outputs or files are consumed by Mentat as trusted input. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so injection risk exists in default workflows.
conditions: IF Devin writes attacker-controlled text into a shared repo or workspace file that Mentat later reads
IF Mentat treats file contents as instructions or prompts without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of shared files as instructions
Use separate workspaces or repos per agent
Add a provenance header to any handoff file
Require manual review before Mentat processes Devin-authored artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and has broad network egress plus Slack/Jira/Notion writes; Mentat reads selected files and sends prompts to a model provider. If they share code or workspace data, sensitive content can flow from Devin into Mentat’s backend or outputs. The profiles do not show isolation strong enough to rule this out.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or repository files
IF Devin places chat, tracker, or docs content into files that Mentat sends to its model provider
mitigations: Keep Devin and Mentat on separate repositories
Restrict Mentat to non-sensitive files only
Redact secrets before either agent processes shared artifacts
Turn off sync of chat/issue/doc exports into the coding workspace

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and modify git state, and Mentat shares state via filesystem while Devin supports parallel sessions with shared integrations. In a shared repo, concurrent edits and git mutations can collide without locking, causing lost work or inconsistent branches. This is a default-dangerous overlap, not a niche edge case.
conditions: IF Devin and Mentat operate on the same git checkout or branch
IF neither orchestrator enforces file or git locks
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch
Serialize git writes through one operator
Enable file locking or checkout locking
Have one agent produce patches only, not direct commits

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin can autonomously act in a cloud workspace and write to GitHub, Slack, Linear, Jira, and Notion; Mentat proposes diffs from selected files. If Devin’s output is fed into Mentat or vice versa without verification, errors can cascade into commits or external actions. The pair’s default autonomy makes this more than a simple review workflow.
conditions: IF Devin-generated text is used as authoritative input for Mentat edits
IF Mentat diffs are applied or Devin’s actions are executed without human verification
mitigations: Require human approval before applying diffs
Add a verification step that checks Devin outputs against source files
Limit Devin to drafting only for external actions
Use a separate reviewer agent for final sign-off

E_compliance.rationale: Devin touches team chat, issue trackers, and docs and can write to Slack/Jira/Notion; Mentat processes selected source files and sends them to a model provider. If regulated or sensitive data is present in the shared workflow, differing retention or residency policies can create compliance gaps. The profiles do not document matching controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Devin-managed integrations and then into Mentat prompts
IF the model provider or SaaS integrations retain data longer than the operator’s policy
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from shared coding tasks
Review retention settings for Slack, Jira, Notion, and model provider
Use synthetic or scrubbed examples for agent workflows
Document a data-handling policy for both agents
